contract.goal: One caller-preference contract in web-core - the caller's locale and zone, resolved from a stored setting then the request headers then configuration, reachable from a MapStruct mapper without threading a parameter and bindable onto a worker thread - replacing the container-zone answer LocaleContextHolder.getTimeZone() gives today and the hard-coded UTC in export.
contract.output: ru.ludwigandreas.webcore.preference (UserPreferences, UserPreferenceSource, UserPreferenceResolver, RequestHeaderPreferenceSource, ConfiguredPreferenceSource, UserPreferenceLocaleContextResolver, UserPreferenceFormatter, package-info); WebCoreProperties.Preferences + WebCorePreferenceAutoConfiguration; StoredUserPreferenceSource in user-settings; ReportCaller.preferences() and SecurityReportCaller in export; RuleGroup.PRESENTATION with noAmbientDefaultLocaleOrZone and noSecondCallerPreferenceType in architecture-rules; READMEs in both locales for three modules; CHANGELOG both locales; docs/harness-enforcement.md rows; the CLAUDE.md one-mechanism paragraph.
constraints: No new in-repo dependency edge: the SPI is declared in web-core and implemented in user-settings, which already depends on web-core. web-core's in-repo dependency count must stay zero.
web-core acquires no persistence dependency, and no cache of its own - SettingsLookup is already backed by cache-spring-boot-starter and a second cache primitive fails RuleGroup.CACHING.
No third-party dependency and no POM change: every type named is in java.base, spring-core, spring-context or spring-webmvc, all already declared. web-core must not take a MapStruct dependency.
UserPreferences holds exactly a Locale and a ZoneId. Anything derivable is a method on it; anything else is a SettingDefinition in the module that needs it.
The stored source answers only for layers more specific than PLATFORM. Answering from DEFAULT would make every caller UTC and make the two sources below it unreachable.

notification-service's RecipientPreferences is NOT consolidated into this contract - it is a subject's preferences on a worker thread with no caller, and the ArchUnit restatement rule must not fire on it.
No relaxation to make a build pass: no weakened Checkstyle or ArchUnit rule, no disabled test, no exemption added to make a real violation of the new rules disappear.
Both locales of every README and CHANGELOG, with the same heading set.

decisions: Pre-implementation: AcceptHeaderLocaleResolver was confirmed by javap on spring-webmvc 6.1.14 to extend AbstractLocaleResolver and to declare no resolveLocaleContext, so LocaleContextHolder.getTimeZone() on a request thread returns TimeZone.getDefault() today. The whole change rests on this and it was verified rather than assumed.

Pre-implementation: DefaultSettingsLookup already holds a LudwigCache<SettingsSubject, ResolvedSettings>, so the stored source is a cache read per request and must add no cache. Verified by reading the class, not inferred from the module README.

Pre-implementation: ResolvedValue.layer() and SettingLayer.isMoreSpecificThan exist, which is what makes the PLATFORM/DEFAULT abstention expressible. Without them the stored source would have had no way to distinguish 'the user chose UTC' from 'nobody has ever set this'.

1.x: UserPreferences.current() reads LocaleContextHolder and prefers our own UserPreferenceLocaleContext over the generic TimeZoneAwareLocaleContext branch, because TimeZone.getTimeZone(zone).toZoneId() is not an identity - a ZoneOffset goes in and a GMT+hh:mm zone id comes out. The carrier type is also what makes currentIfResolved() answerable at all: a SimpleTimeZoneAwareLocaleContext built from defaults and one built from a user's stored choice are the same object.

1.7: the AcceptHeaderLocaleResolver did NOT have to be edited. WebCorePreferenceAutoConfiguration is declared before WebCoreLocalizationAutoConfiguration and registers the localeResolver bean name, and the existing bean is @ConditionalOnMissingBean(name = "localeResolver"), so it backs off by the same ordering mechanism it already uses to win over Spring Boot's. ludwig.web.preferences.enabled=false then restores the old resolver with no further wiring. tasks.md 1.7 describes an edit that turned out to be unnecessary.

2.2: the stored source is registered whenever a SettingsLookup exists and abstains per dimension by asking SettingDefinitionRegistry.find, rather than being kept out of the context by a @Conditional. A condition cannot inspect a registry that has not been built yet, and a silently absent bean is indistinguishable from a deliberate choice; abstaining out loud, named in the startup line, is the only form of this a person debugging 'my saved timezone does nothing' can see. The spec scenario was rewritten to match the code.

3.2: nothing to change in DefaultExecutionPlanner. It already builds RenderContext from request.locale()/request.zone(), and ReportRunController.toRequest already falls back to caller.locale()/caller.zone(); fixing SecurityReportCaller therefore fixed the render context too, and the explicit RunReportRequest.timeZone still wins. Task 3.2 is satisfied by 3.1 rather than by an edit.

4.2 FINDING, measured not reasoned: noClasses().should(<a condition that reports only violations>) checks NOTHING. ArchUnit wraps the condition in never(), which inverts each event, so a notXxx helper from ArchitectureConditions produces zero findings under noClasses() while the rule still reports as passed. Probed directly against the bad.presentation fixture: notDependOnClassesThat(Locale) -> 0 violations and notCallMethods(ZoneId.systemDefault) -> 0 violations, over 5 imported classes that provably have both. Two pre-existing rules were written that way and were inert: CachingRules.noPrivateCaffeineCache (the one-caching-primitive guard) and KafkaRules.noPrivateDeadLetterRecoverer. Both switched to classes().should(...), the reason written at each site, and PresentationRulesTest asserts the violation is REPORTED rather than asserting only that the rule ran - which is the test shape that would have caught this.

4.3: the working rules in this library (AuditRules, OperationVocabularyRules) use the opposite pattern - a custom ArchCondition emitting new SimpleConditionEvent(item, matches, ...) under noClasses(), where the inversion is what makes it fire. noSecondCallerPreferenceType follows that pattern and fired first time; noAmbientDefaultLocaleOrZone uses the helper and needed classes(). Both patterns are correct, and mixing them is what hid the defect: the two shapes look interchangeable in a diff.

4.3 REVISED, by the full reactor build rather than by review: the first noSecondCallerPreferenceType asked only that a class declare both a Locale field and a ZoneId field, with a subject-field-name exemption. mvn clean install reported exactly two violations, both legitimate code - notification-service's RecipientPreferences and StoredPreferences, which carry the pair alongside QuietHours, DigestMode and OptOutMatrix and have no field named like a subject, so the name heuristic never fired. The same rule would also have flagged export's ReportRequest, a fifteen-field request DTO. Discriminator changed to 'the declared non-static instance fields are EXACTLY a Locale and a ZoneId and nothing else', which is what a restatement actually is; the subject-name list is kept as a second clause so the intent survives a later widening. Static fields are skipped so a record declaring its own NONE constant is judged on its components. A SubjectPreferences fixture modelled on RecipientPreferences is now asserted NOT to fire.

4.3: the accepted limit, written at the rule: a third field evades it. Accepted for the reason CachingRules accepts its own name heuristic - the rule exists to catch the reasonable local decision, not the determined evasion, and a rule broad enough for the second would flag every domain object in the platform and be switched off within a quarter.

4.x: export's RenderContext(Locale, ZoneId) was the clearest restatement in the repository and is now record RenderContext(UserPreferences). It is NOT flagged by the rule today either way, because export runs its own ExportArchitectureTest rather than the shared @AnalyzeArchitecture suite - only object-storage, file-ingest, messaging, user-settings, notification-service and crud-service-example run the shared groups. Consolidated anyway rather than left alone, because a design that claims one mechanism while the clearest duplicate survives behind a module that does not run the check is a claim the next reader cannot trust. locale() and zone() are kept as accessors over the held pair, so the change touched one construction site in main code instead of twenty-one call sites, and RenderContext.of(locale, zone) exists for the planner and the tests - a canonical (Locale, ZoneId) constructor would have made the record declare the pair again, which is the restatement itself.

4.x: the full build also confirmed the OTHER new rule has nothing to fix - noAmbientDefaultLocaleOrZone passed across every module that runs the shared suite, so nothing in the platform was reading Locale.getDefault() or ZoneId.systemDefault() on a presentation path. The rule lands as a fence rather than as a cleanup, and that is worth recording so a later reader does not go looking for the violations it must have found.

4.x: the newly-armed CachingRules.noPrivateCaffeineCache also passed ('caching 2' in notification-service's report), so arming the inert rule revealed no hidden violation either. Both facts matter for the same reason: an inert rule that is armed and then passes is only reassuring if somebody checked that it CAN fail, which is what PresentationRulesTest asserts for the new rules.

A background-task notification reports the exit code of the whole shell pipeline, not of maven. 'Verify export after the consolidation' was reported as exit code 0 while the log said BUILD FAILURE with a compile error, because the command ended in a grep. Read the log, never the notification's exit code.

GATE, final: mvn -q validate exits 0; mvn clean install with no flags and no exclusions is BUILD SUCCESS across all 31 reactor entries with Docker up, 2255 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; check_aggregate_report.py reports 27 of 27 jar modules at 72.5% instruction / 61.7% branch; openspec validate passes. Both new ArchUnit rules were confirmed as 'passed, 0 violations' by reading target/architecture-report.json in notification-service, user-settings and crud-service-example rather than inferred from a green build.
failures: scripts/check_api_baseline.sh FAILS, and it is pre-existing rather than caused by this change: a v1.1.0 tag exists locally while distributionManagement points at the placeholder host nexus.example.internal, so all 25 modules in that tag are reported UNRESOLVED. This is the previous change's unresolved task 8.2 - the baseline was never published because -Pci and deploy are denied to agents and there are no credentials. The consequence for this change is that revapi's verdict on it is 'no differences against an empty archive', which is weaker than a real compatibility check. Not worked around, not suppressed, recorded.
